predecessors.name: Satavahana dynasty
predecessors.text: the Telugu coast, once Satavahana land; infobox 'Preceded by: Kalabhra and Satavahana dynasties'

successors.name: Chola Empire
successors.text: the Pallava lands that Cliopatria's Chola Empire shape of 898 covers

successors.name: Western Ganga dynasty
successors.text: the Ganga share of the Pallava legacy: 'the dynasty of the Ganga-Pallavas postulated by the Epigraphists' (Pallava page)

ledger.x: c. 353: the Cholas drive the Pallavas out of Kanchi. 'The Cholas drove the Pallavas away from Kanchi in the mid-4th century, in the reign of Vishnugopa' (chronology 350-355). The page names the Cholas; Cliopatria's Early Chola row ended in 305. Cliopatria's Pallava shape of 353 lacks the Kanchi country.

c. 353: the Andhra coast goes to the Gupta shape. Samudragupta page: he defeated Vishnugopa of Kanchi and the kings of Pishtapura, Kottura, Vengi, Palakka (Ugrasena, possibly a Pallava viceroyalty) and Devarashtra, listed as captured and then released. Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 353 takes 116 cells of its old Pallava…

c. 575: Simhavishnu takes the Tamil country up to the Kaveri from the Kalabhras. Kalabhra page: Simhavishnu 'consolidated his kingdom up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE' and the Kalabhra rule 'had ended for certain by the last quarter of 6th century'; Simhavishnu page: he 'overthrew the Kalabhras and conquered the…

c. 602: the northern provinces go to the Chalukyas. Mahendravarman I page: 'the Chalukya monarch Pulakeshin II attacked the Pallava realm'; 'The Pallavas fought a series of wars in the northern Vengi region' and 'Although Mahendravarman saved his capital, he lost the northern provinces to Pulakeshin.' Pullalur is not…
897: the last Pallava king falls to the Cholas.

wars.name: Samudragupta's southern campaign (Dakshinapatha)
wars.outcome: Samudragupta defeated Vishnugopa of Kanchi and the kings of Pishtapura, Vengi and Kottura and released them; Cliopatria's Gupta shape of 353 holds 116 cells of the Pallava coast.

wars.name: Chola expulsion of the Pallavas from Kanchi
wars.outcome: The Cholas drove the Pallavas away from Kanchi in Vishnugopa's reign.

wars.name: Kadamba-Pallava contest
wars.outcome: Mayurasharma 'defeated the armies of the Pallavas of Kanchi' and the Pallava king 'condescended to recognize the growing might of the Kadambas' (Kadamba dynasty page); the Mayurasharma page has the Pallavas under Skandavarman 'recognised him as a sovereign'…

wars.name: Simhavishnu's war on the Kalabhras
wars.outcome: Simhavishnu overthrew the Kalabhras and held the land up to the Kaveri; he then fought the Pandyas and Ceylon.

wars.name: Pallava-Chalukya wars: Pulakeshin II and Mahendravarman I
wars.outcome: Pulakeshin II attacked the Pallava realm; Mahendravarman I 'decimated his chief enemies at Pullalur' and saved his capital but lost the northern provinces.

wars.name: Narasimhavarman I's war on Pulakeshin II
wars.outcome: Narasimhavarman I defeated the Chalukyas in several battles, including Manimangalam, and took Vatapi, killing Pulakeshin II in 642; 'The city was never a capital again.'

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is on any page opened; the Krishna-Pennar line (Skandavarman), the Kaveri limit (Simhavishnu) and the 'northern provinces' lost to the Chalukyas are described, not surveyed.
